subject: Proposal: annual prepayment with safety-net and ramp mechanics
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Shivam Rao <shivam@coralanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Switch to annual prepayment — quick options and safety-net

Hi Shivam —

Great talking earlier. Per our conversation I pulled together a compact set of options for Coral if you want to move from monthly invoicing to an annual prepay. High level asks from my side so we can tailor the numbers:
- current ARR / average monthly spend (rough)
- expected growth trajectory over next 12 months (percent)
- appetite for multi-year vs single-year lock

What I’m proposing to start the discussion:
1) 12-month prepay at a tiered discount (examples below) with an attached safety-net: if monthly usage drops below a defined threshold in the first 90 days, unused prepay converts into credits that amortize over the next 6 months (not a cash refund).
2) Optional 24-month variant with slightly deeper discount but a smaller safety-net window.
3) Lift-and-shift billing: invoice up-front for the prepay; usage above committed units billed monthly.

If you can share current average monthly spend and a preferred committed level, I’ll run concrete numbers. I attached a short PDF with example math and a one-page SOW stub.

Proposed next steps:
- You share April/May billing snapshot (one-line)
- We propose two concrete term sheets you can review with procurement
- Legal/finance can draft the one-line rollback clause for review

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps — available tomorrow after 11am PT.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20260503-jasmine-prepay-proposal.pdf (pdf)
From: Shivam Rao <shivam@coralanalytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@coralanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Switch to annual prepayment — quick options and safety-net

Jasmine — thanks for the quick follow-up and the deck. A few data points from our side:
- Current blended monthly spend: ~$28,000 (we had a spike in March from a pilot)
- Expect flat-to-modest growth (5–10%) across H2; Q1 next year is our risk window (we historically see a drop-off when a product line sunsets)
- Preference: we like the predictability of annual prepay, but procurement will need a mechanism to avoid being stuck with a large prepay if usage meaningfully drops early in the term.

Specific asks from procurement/legal that would ease the move:
- A short “rollback safety-net” (30–90 days) where, if average daily token consumption falls >40% below the committed baseline, Coral can either convert unused prepay to pro-rated cash credit or opt to revert to monthly billing with a defined reconciliation.
- If a cash refund is not possible, a clear credit amortization schedule (6–9 months) and a cap on credits applied to future invoices (so credits don’t block us for years).

We’d like a proposal that shows both: (A) 1-year prepay with a 90-day safety-net (credit route) and (B) 2-year prepay with 60-day safety-net. Also include how discounts change if we pay the second year upfront in year one.

Can you include a sample legal clause we can show our GC? If you can get a proposal by Tuesday EOD, we’ll route to procurement immediately.

—Shivam
CTO, Coral Analytics
shivam@coralanalytics.com

On Sun, May 3, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message]
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Shivam Rao <shivam@coralanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Switch to annual prepayment — quick options and safety-net

Hi Shivam —

Thanks for the details — I’ve sketched two concrete offers below and attached the SOW stub. Numbers use your $28k baseline. These are negotiable; I wanted to give procurement something they can mark up.

Offer A — 12-month single-year prepay (preferred economics if you want quick upside)
- Commit: $300k prepay (≈ 10–11 months of current run-rate)
- Discount: 20% off list inference unit rate
- Safety-net: 90-day measurement period starting on go-live; if average monthly consumption during those 90 days is >40% below the committed baseline, unused prepay converts to a credit pool equal to the unused dollar value. Credits are applied monthly over the following 6 months (max 50% of monthly invoice can be offset by credits). No cash refunds.
- Billing: invoice due on signature (net 30)
- Conversion: Customer can elect to revert to monthly billing after the 90-day window with 45 days’ notice; a 15% conversion fee on the remaining prepay value applies.

Offer B — 24-month prepay (lower unit cost, longer commitment)
- Commit: $520k prepay (year 1 & 2 billed upfront)
- Discount: 26% off list rate for year 1; year 2 rate locked but no further retroactive credits if usage declines after year 1
- Safety-net: 60-day measurement window only; unused value converts to credits amortized over 9 months.

Other notes and rationale:
- We prefer credit amortization versus cash refund because it aligns incentives toward usage while protecting both parties.
- If you need cash refund language for procurement, we can propose a capped refund (up to 25% of unused prepay) but it will materially reduce the overall discount.

Next ask from our side: please confirm whether procurement requires refunds vs credits (and the preferred cap if any). If you’re comfortable with Offer A as a starting point, I’ll loop in finance and legal to draft the one-line rollback/safety-net clause for your GC to review.

Call availability: Tue 5/5 10:30–11:30 PT or 3–4pm PT — let me know what works and I’ll calendar.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Coral_SOW_v1.pdf
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Switch to annual prepayment — quick options and safety-net

Jas —

Nice framing. A few tactical points from pricing/ops perspective before we surface to customer:
1) If procurement insists on cash refunds, include a tiered refund cap: 0–15% unused => no refund, 15–40% unused => credit-only, >40% unused => capped cash refund at 20% of unused value. That preserves economics and gives procurement a true escape hatch.
2) For Offer A, propose a 3-month fully-guaranteed safety-net (customer can elect refund/credits per the cap above) to win the deal; offset cost with a smaller increase to the conversion fee (20% conversion fee instead of 15%).
3) Include an operational clause that unused credits expire after 12 months post-amortization to prevent long tail liability.
4) Request a one-page procurement questionnaire from Coral with expected monthly token profile (90-day granularity) — Laura, can you push the questionnaire template and calendar the 5/5 10:30 PT call if they confirm?

If Coral prefers a true monthly fallback (revert to monthly billing immediately), we should require a minimum 6-week notice and a reconciliation invoice to reconcile actual usage vs committed prepay at day of revert.

I’ll draft language for the ‘refund cap’ and the conversion-fee tweak — Jasmine, happy to share a tracked clause for their GC. Also add the HubSpot deal link: https://hubspot.example/deal/CORAL-2026-PREPAY-01.

- Aditya
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

[Internal-only guidance: our finance threshold for offering any cash refund is $50k+ of unused value; below that we will default to credit-only.]
